source.title: Enabling Federated Inference via Unsupervised Consensus Embedding
source.authors: Yui Hashimoto; Takayuki Nishio; Yuichi Kitagawa; Takahito Tanimura

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether independently trained models’ representations can be aligned through learned mappings, using a consensus-embedding method rather than a natural-convergence or scale-sweep measure.
record.gate_note: The study deliberately trains consensus-embedding layers to align representations. It does not test whether alignment emerges as models grow or improve, or whether vision and language representations naturally converge. Its t-SNE analyses explicitly describe alignment after training; the forced-unification ablation also reports its effect on inference accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study trains a two-layer nonlinear contrastive mapping (CE layer) to force heterogeneous encoders' features into a shared space. It reports that mapping's success as part of its own federated-inference method. The evidence is qualitative t-SNE plus downstream accuracy of CE-FI. It does not measure whether independently trained representations are interchangeable by a simple map, or how much is lost compared with a direct cross-model transfer. The alignment is induced by training, so it is a tool, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that CE-FI consistently beats solo inference and in many settings approaches input-sharing and shared-encoder FI without sharing inputs or parameters. They identify representation alignment in the CE layer as the primary performance bottleneck, especially in scratch-trained settings, with OOD data in CO training not a major factor. Reconstruction attacks do not trivially recover inputs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses learned nonlinear consensus-embedding and cooperative-output layers trained for federated inference; it does not reproduce a natural-convergence measurement recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment quality and inference results vary with dataset and training setting: MNIST scratch embeddings are more clearly structured than CIFAR-10 scratch embeddings; the authors also report differing gains from embedding unification across pretrained and scratch settings.

fits_no_version.finding: A two-layer MLP trained contrastively on shared unlabeled data maps features from encoders with different pretraining objectives (supervised, CLIP, DINOv3) and architectures (ViT, ResNet-50, ConvNeXtV2) into a common space. Same-input embeddings land close together in t-SNE. Alignment stays imperfect and is weaker for scratch CIFAR-10. Forcing perfect unification raises accuracy more in the scratch setting than with pretrained encoders.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heterogeneous encoders' features can be aligned into a shared space by a jointly trained contrastive nonlinear projection. Alignment quality depends on the semantic quality of each encoder's features.

record.problems: The alignment evidence is qualitative t-SNE interpretation rather than a numerical representation-similarity measure. Alignment is explicitly induced by training the CE layer. The embedding-unification results are shown only in a figure, with no numeric values stated in the text. The study does not examine scaling or model capability.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results identified beyond the alignment visualizations and embedding-unification ablations recorded above. Other reported classification, communication, and reconstruction results do not directly measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no natural-alignment measure.
No image–caption alignment. CLIP is used only as an image encoder.
No measured loss of a simple, linear or stitching map between models. The shared space is learned jointly with a contrastive objective.
No comparison of similarity metrics. The CIFAR-100 shared-data domain-shift test measures accuracy of the method, not representation similarity.
No measure of natural alignment levels or their causes. The remark that pretrained encoders are 'more naturally aligned' is speculation, not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'tests' and its supports/limits_scope labels are withdrawn. The alignment is the optimisation target of the study's own method, it is shown only by t-SNE and downstream accuracy, and the map is not a fixed simple cross-model map whose loss is measured. Li et al. (arXiv:1511.07543) is cited only as background for heterogeneous feature spaces. Heterogeneous-architecture accuracy varies by which device produces the embedding, which the authors attribute to how well each encoder aligns; this is not quantified per encoder in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no measurement of naturally emerging alignment across independently trained models.
No paired image-caption vision-language alignment or comparison of alignment with model performance.
No same-architecture, different-initialization study of shared features or subspaces.

The study maps representations into a learned shared space, but does not test linear mapping, stitching, relative representations, mapping without paired inputs, or a direct measure of representation-transfer loss.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified across models.
No systematic comparison of similarity metrics, metric settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution representation similarity.
No test of whether naturally occurring alignment plateaus or is explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: CE-FI consensus embeddings (three-device Unified-architecture ViT setting; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared intermediate features and learned consensus embeddings in t-SNE visualizations; the CE layer was trained to align embeddings for the same input.
rows.measure: Qualitative cross-device representation alignment and class-wise structure
rows.baseline: Intermediate features from different devices are described as highly inconsistent and not directly comparable in a shared space.
rows.value: After the CE layer, embeddings for the same input are described as nearby across devices; coarse class-wise clustering is also observed.
rows.note: Qualitative t-SNE interpretation; no numerical similarity score is reported. The alignment is deliberately trained, not naturally emergent.
rows.check: Qualitative t-SNE of the study's own trained contrastive CE layer (ImageNet-supervised, CLIP and DINOv3 ViTs, CIFAR-100). The alignment is the training objective, not a measured cross-model mapping loss. No similarity number is given.

rows.subject: CE-FI consensus embeddings (scratch-trained models; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared individual feature spaces with learned consensus embedding spaces using t-SNE.
rows.measure: Qualitative cross-device alignment and class-wise clustering
rows.baseline: Individual feature space shows well-separated class clusters, including for unseen classes.
rows.value: Class-wise clustering remains clear, and embeddings from different devices for the same sample are described as nearly identical locations.
rows.note: Aggregate visualization across devices; no numerical similarity measure is given.
rows.check: Same issue on scratch MNIST, Dirichlet α=0.1: a diagnostic of the study's own method with no quantitative measure. Fig. 12 is captioned for 'pretrained models' but is described in the scratch section.

rows.subject: CE-FI consensus embeddings (scratch-trained models; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared individual feature spaces with learned consensus embedding spaces using t-SNE.
rows.measure: Qualitative cross-device alignment and class-wise separation
rows.baseline: Individual feature space is described as lacking well-formed class-wise clusters, with classes substantially intermixed.
rows.value: Inter-device alignment is achieved to some extent, but class separation is weaker than for MNIST and the pretrained-encoder setting; clusters overlap and show distributional shifts across devices.
rows.note: Aggregate visualization across devices; no numerical similarity measure is given.
rows.check: Scratch CIFAR-10 (ResNet-18) t-SNE: weaker class separation and partial alignment, qualitative only. This is a diagnostic of the study's own method.

rows.subject: CE-FI (pretrained-encoder, Heterogeneous-architecture setting; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: For the CO-layer training and inference, replaced device-specific consensus embeddings with their across-device average to simulate a unified embedding space.
rows.measure: Inference accuracy difference from baseline CE-FI
rows.value: Figure only; the text says unification improves accuracy, with a relatively modest improvement in the pretrained-encoder setting.
rows.note: Reported as an aggregate figure; the text gives no numeric difference. This is a downstream accuracy ablation, not a direct similarity score.
rows.check: Method ablation: replaces the embeddings with their average and reports the accuracy gain (Fig. 14, figure only). This compares variants of the study's own method, not a measure of representation convergence or mapping loss.

rows.subject: CE-FI (scratch setting; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: For the CO-layer training and inference, replaced device-specific consensus embeddings with their across-device average to simulate a unified embedding space.
rows.measure: Inference accuracy difference from baseline CE-FI
rows.value: Figure only; the text says unification improves accuracy, with a particularly pronounced improvement in the scratch setting.
rows.note: Reported as an aggregate figure; the text gives no numeric difference. This is a downstream accuracy ablation, not a direct similarity score.
rows.check: Same method ablation (scratch CIFAR-10, Moderate/Disjoint, figure only). Not a measure of any version's effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Learned consensus mappings in the CIFAR-100 unified-architecture setting and MNIST scratch setting
reader_labels.reason: The study reports nearby or nearly identical same-input embeddings across devices after learned mapping (r1, r2). This supports mapping into a shared representation space in these tested settings, not the broader claims about simple linear maps or low transfer loss.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 scratch setting and the embedding-unification ablations
reader_labels.reason: The CIFAR-10 scratch visualization shows only partial alignment and weak class separation (r3); forced unification improves inference accuracy, but the reported effect is qualitative and does not establish near-lossless transfer (r4, r5).
